highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156 improves platform support and native reliability while incorporating the latest Skia m156 fixes.
highlights_body: This release updates Apple and Uno support, strengthens Linux and WebAssembly native packaging, and fixes stream, string, image-copy, and Android rendering behavior.

bullets.detail: The bundled renderer includes the current upstream Chrome m156 bug-fix syncs.

bullets.lead: String and native data conversion hardened
bullets.detail: StringUtilities now validates Unicode character codes and string inputs correctly, while native C-string conversion avoids reading past its source buffer and writes directly to SKData.
Front-buffered streams no longer retain data unnecessarily, and managed image pixel copies avoid avoidable overhead.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: Texture rendering is synchronized with display refresh to improve Android presentation behavior.
HarfBuzz feature-string handling no longer allocates native memory while preserving existing decoding behavior.

bullets.lead: HarfBuzz UTF-32 encoding uses pooled buffers
bullets.detail: HarfBuzzSharp reuses encoding buffers to reduce allocation pressure when processing UTF-32 text.

bullets.lead: Uno WinUI support updated for Uno Platform 7
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Views.Uno.WinUI now builds against Uno Platform 7.

bullets.lead: Native assets aligned across Apple, Windows, Linux, and WebAssembly
bullets.detail: Apple deployment targets and Windows dependencies align with current .NET platform requirements; Linux binds bundled HarfBuzz locally, and WebAssembly packages the required WebGPU implementation in libSkiaSharp.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Bundled the WebGPU implementation for WebAssembly and updated the Uno WinUI view package for Uno Platform 7
contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Bound the bundled HarfBuzz functions locally on Linux and stabilized Blazor CPU sample startup tests
contributor_summaries.dalexsoto: Addressed contextual policy-check findings in CI
